title: listings.rename_feature_keys
description: Second half of a feature-slug rename: move the KEYS of stored drafts to follow a category schema that renamed a feature. A catalogue import that renames a slug in place (make_ref_select -> make) moves the schema and nothing else; every listing composed against the old schema keeps its answer under the old key in features_draft, so the facet empties, the search projection loses the value, and listings_reproject_features on its own would DROP it (it keys on current slugs). This call rewrites the key in place across the category subtree (resolved over categories.children, because a feature defined on a parent is inherited downward), keeps the value untouched, re-projects the touched categories through the same code path as listings_reproject_features, and lets those writes emit listing.updated so a search index re-pulls. A draft that already answers the NEW key as well as the old one is NEVER guessed at: both keys are left exactly as they are and the pair is reported in `conflicts`. Idempotent — a second run finds nothing to move. This object validates the request payload; the response is {listings_scanned, listings_changed, keys_renamed, conflicts: [{listing_id, old, new}], conflicts_total, conflicts_truncated, categories, subtree_resolved, deleted_skipped, dry_run, reprojected}.

category_id.description: Root of the subtree to rewrite. Its descendants are included: a feature defined on a parent category is answered by listings in every category beneath it.

renames.description: {old_slug: new_slug}. Refused as a whole (nothing read, nothing written) when it is empty, renames a slug onto itself, sends two old slugs to one new one, or chains (a slug appearing on both sides) — every one of those makes the outcome depend on iteration order.

dry_run.description: Report the counts and the conflicts and write nothing. Default false.
